beats.summary: Michael gives a public statement denying any issues with Sabre printers and reacts to media coverage.

evidence.snippet: Michael (on Youtube video): There is nothing wrong, nor will there ever be wrong with any Sabre printers. Case closed.
Michael: Apparently, there are allegations that Sabre printers can cause a fire. So they asked me to give a statement to the press.

beats.summary: Jo confronts the office about a whistleblower leaking printer defects to the press and demands the culprit come forward.

evidence.snippet: Jo: Turns out our printers are famous. They're all over the news.

beats.summary: The office is pressured to deny involvement and sign forms stating innocence regarding the whistleblower incident.

evidence.snippet: Jo (as Gabe hands out forms to everyone): It's a little form, says "I did not do it."
Michael: There is no reason for anyone here to sign this, because I know everything there is to know about these people.

beats.summary: Michael and Jo discuss harsh consequences for the whistleblower if caught.

evidence.snippet: Jo: So say we catch this whistleblower, what do you think I should do with him?
Michael: We should give him a one-way ticket to Montego Bay, where they keep all the al-Qaeda.

beats.summary: The office computers are searched by lawyers for information on the leak, causing tension among employees.

evidence.snippet: Oscar: The lawyers are searching our hard drives for information on the leak.
Nick: Yeah. I already got to yours, Kevin.

beats.summary: Andy denies being the whistleblower despite accusations from coworkers.

evidence.snippet: Angela: Everybody knows it was Andy, and it is not fair for us all to take the fall for his big stupid mouth!
Andy: I, I didn't know. I didn't do that!
